disclaimer: General information, not medical advice. Effects of the cycle on performance are small on average and differ a lot between people. Talk to a clinician about missed periods, severe pain or heavy bleeding.

phases.notice: Energy and comfort vary a lot. Some feel fine, some feel low energy or cramps.
phases.adjustment: Train as planned if you feel good. If not, lower the load or reps, shorten the session, or swap to a recovery day.

phases.notice: Many feel more energetic as the cycle progresses.
phases.adjustment: Good window to push a heavy or high-effort day if you feel ready.

phases.notice: Some feel strong, some notice looser joints or a dip in coordination.
phases.adjustment: Warm up well, control landings and cutting movements, and use the Low Impact swap if a joint feels unstable.

phases.notice: Higher effort feel, poorer sleep, bloating or mood changes are common late in this phase.
phases.adjustment: Keep training. Use RIR to pace sets, extend rest between sets, and keep deload and recovery days honest.

phases.phase: No cycle, irregular, menopause or hormonal contraception
phases.notice: Patterns differ and may not follow these phases.
phases.adjustment: Ignore the phases. Use how you feel on the day, sleep and stress as the guide.
